name: pdk-appointment-availability-staleness-budget
instr:
We need public scheduling to stay responsive without repeatedly fetching an owner's CalDAV calendar, while keeping booking decisions exact. Extend the Python backend in `/app/backend` for CalDAV schedules; the public page is `POST /schedule/public/availability` with `{"url": "<public schedule link>"}`, and requests use `PUT /schedule/public/availability/request` with `{"url": "<link>", "s_a": {"slot": {"start": "<ISO datetime>", "duration": 30}, "attendee": {"email": "<email>", "name": "<name>", "timezone": "UTC"}}}`.

Availability across API instances and Celery workers must use shared per-calendar remote-calendar snapshots (without mixing calendars' busy events) no older than `AVAILABILITY_MAX_STALENESS_SECONDS` (3 seconds here); every successful page response carries a timezone-aware ISO timestamp (with a UTC offset) in `X-Availability-As-Of`. A new remote busy event must appear as a booked slot (its entry stays in `slots` with `booking_status` 3) within 8 seconds (and never from a snapshot older than the budget); read busy time from the remote calendar's events rather than free-busy queries, and note that the existing `CalDavConnector.list_events` keeps its results in Redis for up to `REDIS_EVENT_EXPIRE_SECONDS` (900 seconds), so snapshots need their own fresh fetch, and 20 concurrent reads across two instances of an expired snapshot cause at most one remote calendar fetch per calendar. A Celery worker must be able to refresh an active schedule's snapshot ahead of a page
